analysis.investment_thesis: Cohance (formerly Suven Pharma) is a CDMO/API business experiencing four consecutive years of profit decline alongside collapsing operating margins, yet it trades at an eye-watering EV/EBITDA of 94.7x—the worst valuation-quality mismatch in this cohort. A mid-2025 balance sheet restructuring (total assets nearly tripled to INR 5,568 Cr, borrowings jumped 7x to INR 451 Cr) adds transformation risk that Fisher's framework demands be resolved before any capital commitment.
key_strengths: High gross margin of 71.5% reflects value-added NCE intermediate and oligonucleotide capabilities with pricing power at the molecule level
6-year revenue CAGR of 21.2% shows the underlying addressable market (CDMO, ADC, oligonucleotide) is genuinely growing
OCF has been positive all 5 years and the CWIP build-out (INR 357 Cr) signals meaningful capacity investment
key_risks: Net profit has fallen every year for four years: INR 454 Cr (FY22) → INR 265 Cr (FY25), a 42% cumulative decline
Operating margin has collapsed from ~43% in FY21 to just 8.89% today—cost structure has deteriorated severely
Sudden balance sheet explosion in FY25 (assets +147%, borrowings +594%) signals a major acquisition whose economics and integration risk are opaque
red_flags: EV/EBITDA of 94.7x is not a valuation—it is a speculation premium on an unproven turnaround
Operating income in absolute terms (INR 375 Cr in FY25) is lower than it was in FY21 (INR 443 Cr) despite revenue nearly doubling—management has failed to convert growth into profit
Name change from Suven Pharmaceuticals to Cohance Lifesciences in May 2025 coincides with the balance sheet surge, suggesting a transformative corporate event with limited disclosure
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Fisher's first test for any investment is: does the company have products and processes that will generate sustained profit growth? Cohance fails this test emphatically. Despite 21% revenue CAGR, every key profitability metric has been deteriorating for four years. Operating margin has fallen from the high-40s% to 8.89%—a collapse that suggests rising raw material costs, capacity underutilisation, customer concentration issues, or all three. The CDMO/oligonucleotide business model is strategically sound (pharma outsourcing tailwinds are real), but execution has been poor.

The FY25 balance sheet transformation—total assets nearly tripling, equity jumping from INR 2,051 Cr to INR 3,787 Cr, borrowings surging 7x—points to a major acquisition or merger. Fisher was emphatic: never invest in a restructuring story until you understand exactly what has been acquired and at what price. With an EV/EBITDA of 94.7x, the market is pricing a future that the company has not yet demonstrated the ability to deliver. The forward P/E of 35.9x still assumes a dramatic earnings recovery. Avoid until the restructuring rationale, integration, and margin recovery are demonstrably on track.
